metadata.title: Set it up once
metadata.bookend_exempt_reason: show-tell style (Bear, 2026-09-26): opens on the hesitant writer + terms card, no verdict card; Your Turn is the composer; spoken outro stays.
metadata.audience: smart general audience — pragmatic, not necessarily AI experts; every term explained
metadata.source_doc: NEW — built from scratch 2026-10-03 (no mirror source); facts verified 2026-10-03, see FACTCHECK.md

beats.narration_text: Hallo. This is Liam, in for Bear. You asked: why does the AI forget everything between chats? Wrong question. A new chat is supposed to start fresh. The real question is: how do I make every chat start already knowing me?

show.event: types 'Why does the AI forget everything between chats?'
backspaces 'forget everything between chats' -> 'start every chat already knowing me' on the spoken correction

props.text:
Why does the AI
forget everything
between chats?
props.replacementWords: start every chat already knowing me

beats.motion_claim: The writer types the naive forget-between-chats question and corrects it to the real one: start every chat already knowing me.

qc.sparse_reason: Hesitant-writer bookend: the correction is the motion.

beats.narration_text: Three terms you'll hear. Instructions: saved lines the app reads before every chat. Memory: things the AI itself saves from your chats. And preferences: your standing answers — tone, format, how much you already know.

show.event: 'instructions' lands
'memory' lands
'preferences' lands

terms.meaning: saved lines the app reads before every chat
things the AI itself saves from your chats
your standing answers: tone, format, skill level

qc.sparse_reason: TERMS card: three prerequisites, one line each.

beats.narration_text: Meet the annoyance. You open the AI and ask: explain p-values. Back comes a wall of technical jargon. You're a beginner at statistics, but the AI doesn't know that. This chat started five seconds ago — so you explain yourself. Again.

show.event: chat window fades in with a 'one chat' label
user bubble 'explain p-values' lands
the jargon answer lands line by line
a loop arrow draws and the 'again?' label lands

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell body beat: one window, one exchange, one loop

beats.motion_claim: The jargon answer lands on a stranger chat, then the loop arrow closes the repeat.

beats.narration_text: Now the fix. Most AI apps have a settings page where you can write a few lines about yourself — your standing instructions. The app pins that note to every new chat. It's like a cover page the AI reads before it ever sees your question.

show.event: settings panel fades in with a 'settings' label
the note drops into the panel and the terracotta pin lands
two chat windows fade in on the right
kraft cables draw from the note to each window; 'every chat' lands

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell body beat: the pinned note joins the cast

beats.motion_claim: The note drops into settings, gets pinned, and cables it to every chat.

beats.narration_text: Where is it? Open your AI app's settings, or your profile page. Look for words like instructions, personalization, or memory. Every app names it differently and moves it around — so search for the word, not the button.

show.event: settings panel close-up fades in
three keyword pills land: instructions / personalization / memory
the cursor hovers onto the 'instructions' pill
a terracotta check lands; 'look for these words' label lands

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell body beat: one panel, three words, one choice

beats.motion_claim: The cursor picks 'instructions' out of the three candidate words.

beats.narration_text: What do you write? Good instructions are short and concrete. Three to five lines, each one a standing answer. Keep answers short. I'm a beginner at statistics. Plain English, no jargon. Give me steps I can try today.

show.event: the pinned note fades in with 'the note' label
'keep answers short' writes in with its bullet
'beginner at statistics' writes in with its bullet
'plain English, no jargon' writes in with its bullet
'steps I can try today' writes in with its bullet

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell body beat: the note fills with four short lines

beats.motion_claim: Four concrete lines write themselves onto the note, one per spoken line.

beats.narration_text: Bad instructions are a life story — the AI can't use your biography. Or they contradict themselves: be brief, and explain everything. Two orders that fight. The AI can't obey both — so give it one rule per line.

show.event: the note fades in again, labelled 'the note'
dim scribble lines fill the page and spill off its edge
the 'be brief!' and 'explain everything!' pills land below
a terracotta X lands between the two pills

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell body beat: overflow plus one contradiction

beats.motion_claim: The life story spills off the page; the two orders collide on the X.

beats.narration_text: The payoff. Same question, two chats. Without the note: a wall of jargon. With the note: short, plain, no jargon — written for a beginner. You wrote four lines once. Every chat after that starts informed.

show.event: the 'same question' bar types in on top
both chat windows fade in below, labelled
the jargon answer lands in the left window
the pinned note lands on the right window; the plain answer lands
a terracotta check lands on the right window

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell body beat: two panels, one difference

beats.motion_claim: The same question gets two answers; the note is the only difference.

beats.narration_text: One more kind of line: what you never want. No emojis. No 'as an AI language model.' Don't open with an apology. The AI's habits are yours to set — write down the ones you don't like, and they're gone.

show.event: the pinned note fades in with 'the note' label
'no emojis' lands and is crossed with a terracotta X
'no as an AI' lands and is crossed with a terracotta X
'no sorry-first opens' lands and is crossed with a terracotta X

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell body beat: three bans, three crosses

beats.motion_claim: Three unwanted habits are written down and crossed out.

beats.narration_text: One last thing: it's not set-and-forget. Your needs change, so the note can change. Pull it out, rewrite a line, pin it back. Review it every few months — or the day the answers start feeling off.

show.event: the pinned note fades in with three lines
the note lifts out; the pencil appears
'beginner at statistics' is replaced by 'comfortable with basics'
the 'every few months' pill lands; the note pins back down

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell body beat: the note is edited, not replaced

beats.motion_claim: One line is rewritten and the note pins back into place.

beats.narration_text: And the note follows you. Same instructions on your phone and your computer — wherever you open the app. One setting, written once, shaping every chat you ever start.

show.event: the pinned note fades in at center
the phone and the web window fade in left and right
kraft cables draw from the note to both devices

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell body beat: one note, two devices

beats.motion_claim: The same note feeds the phone and the computer.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Open your AI app's settings and find the instructions page. Then paste this in: I like answers that are short and practical. I'm a beginner at statistics, so explain terms in plain English. No jargon, no filler. Run it on your next question — and notice: the AI is meeting the informed version of you.

show.event: Composer opens — 'Your turn.'
the prompt types in full
two check lines land
